The inline image viewer is problematic, because for users on slower Internet connections —and that's more common that you'd think— there can be significant delays in loading high-resolution images. Worse, the Open link doesn't even appear until the image has loaded. I know power users can middle click the original inline link, which will make the image load in a background tab, but how many people know that? And even if they do, many may think it inconvenient having to deal with another tab and would rather click through to the image in the same tab, which the can't do until it's fully loaded inline, so for those who prefer to view images at their original sites, the inline viewer just gets in the way. There should be a user preference to turn inline viewing off entirely. Btw., the delay often is there again even when the image at the original URL is still in the browser cache: Whenever the thread that the image link occurs in has been reloaded, clicking on an image link caused a new loading delay. Again, the thread has been reloaded but the image is still in the browser cache (and may even still be open in another tab), but simply clicking the line still causes a delay as the inline image viewer apparently tries to load another copy.
